pages.text: Grandpa lowered the shop awning, and the alley lamps came on. "Who will brush before going home?" He set cups beside the water bucket. Kiki, the pointy-eared cat, was already heading home beneath the roof edge.
"I will not! The water is icy!" Kiki grinned, showing teeth. "Look! They are already white as snow!" Then Kiki slipped under the blanket and fell asleep.
The snow had stopped by morning. Kiki yawned, then paused. Something hard was stuck between the back teeth. Even pushing with the tongue would not move it. "I ate roast chestnuts last night..."
At the shop door, Grandpa poured stove-warmed water into the bucket. Steam rose. "It is not icy. Try it." Nono, the smallest, roundest sparrow, and Gugu, the broad-chested pigeon, stood holding cups.
Grandpa set a handful of fresh white snow beside Kiki. "Brush with this beside you. Teeth as white as snow!" Kiki looked at the snow and touched the teeth.
Kiki squeezed toothpaste onto the brush. Up, down, inside, and around the back teeth—brush, brush! Bubbles foamed. Pop! A bit of chestnut shell came free.
Kiki rinsed and opened wide. The teeth shone! Beside the handful of snow, they were just as white. "Teeth as white as snow!"
"Your brushed teeth look like the morning snow!" Grandpa chuckled. Kiki's mouth felt fresh, bringing smile after smile. Kiki touched the green bell at the neck.
That night, Kiki reached the bucket first. "One, brush before bed! Two, brush again in the morning! Three, brush inside too!" Nono and Gugu made bubbles alongside.
Grandpa stroked Kiki's forehead. Daily brushing keeps teeth white as snow. "See? Still white today! Teeth as white as snow!" Kiki grinned.
